clue.text: Degree was 0K, though very far from hot

definitions.text: Degree was 0K, though very far from hot

blocks.note: surface reading: a temperature that was all right, oddly described as far from hot
setter's reading: 0K means zero kelvin, the coldest temperature possible

explanation.surface: Someone reports a temperature as fine, yet somehow nowhere near warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read OK as 0K, zero on the Kelvin scale, and the paradox vanishes: that reading is the lowest temperature physics allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero kelvin is the theoretical floor of temperature, about minus 273 Celsius, as cold as anything can be.

clue.text: Goddess as a beginner lacks finish

indicators.note: lacking a finish means the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a starter is one who begins

explanation.surface: A goddess still learning the ropes never quite completes anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician deity of fertility and love, worshipped across the ancient Near East.

clue.text: Wood, river Commissioner

blocks.note: first meaning: red sandalwood, a dye timber
second meaning: the District Commissioner hero of Edgar Wallace's ... of the River

explanation.walkthrough: Wood and river look like a geography list, but they are two separate meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Red sanders is a sandalwood timber, and Sanders is the colonial official in Edgar Wallace's African stories.

clue.text: No end of such trouble with mill-sites

indicators.note: trouble suggests things thrown into disorder, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Industrial sites bring endless headaches to the people who run them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boundless has no limit, so there is an infinite supply, never running out.

clue.text: A link with a song of unrequited love

blocks.note: first meaning: a link was a flaming brand carried to light the streets
second meaning: the word names a sad ballad of love not returned

explanation.walkthrough: Link here is the old word for a flaming brand, not a chain loop; a torch song is a lament for love not returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Torch covers both a carried flame for lighting the way and, in torch song, a lovelorn ballad.

clue.text: Brewer's last word or almost so

definitions.text: Brewer's last word or almost so

blocks.note: surface reading: a brewer's final remark, or the end of Brewer's dictionary
setter's reading: the science of fermentation, which comes nearly last in alphabetical word lists

explanation.surface: A brewer gets nearly the final say in a discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the study of brewing, and it sits at or near the end of most dictionaries, hence last word, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Zymurgy is the branch of chemistry dealing with fermentation in brewing and winemaking.

clue.text: New edition of Lear is initially easy to sell

indicators.note: a new edition rearranges the material that follows into fresh form
initially points to the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of easy

explanation.surface: A publisher hopes a fresh edition of King Lear will move off the shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into cash, that is, to sell it.

clue.text: Magic aircraft shot down by this politician?

blocks.note: a magic carpet flies in the Arabian Nights
a hunter who bags game shoots it down

explanation.surface: A politician is accused of downing a flying carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a carpetbagger is read as one who bags carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpetbaggers were outsiders, originally Northerners in the post-war South, who stood for office where they had no roots.

clue.text: Mark 1,000, meaning just the opposite

blocks.note: Mark Antony, Roman general
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A score of a thousand marks turns out to signify its reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is a first name here: drop it and keep the Roman's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word whose sense is contrary to another, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Search for the odd sorcerer

blocks.note: rum is British slang for strange
a mage is a magician

explanation.surface: Someone goes hunting for an eccentric wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things untidily, looking for something lost.

clue.text: Choose Manx Dick -- 'e's no follower of the dogs

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the following word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
Dick is a short form of Richard
dropped-aitch spelling of he

explanation.surface: A Manx man named Dick is picked, but he's no fan of the greyhounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx looks like it says Dick comes from the Isle of Man; it means tailless, after the island's tailless cats.
explanation.definitionFit: In greyhound racing a mechanical lure runs ahead of the dogs, so it leads and never trails them.

clue.text: Lead astray through the green

blocks.note: per means by way of
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone guides a walker off course across the village green.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert someone is to corrupt them, steering them from the right path.

clue.text: First lady in romance or maybe in a German poet

indicators.note: maybe hints the word before it might appear in another order
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: Heinrich Heine, German Romantic poet
the two letters swapped round

explanation.surface: A romance's leading lady may appear inside a German poet's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The female lead of a story is its principal woman character, so she has top billing.

clue.text: Hardy lass seen round river lock

indicators.note: seen round means the named girl encircles the next letter

blocks.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's heroine
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: One of Hardy's heroines is spotted by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy lass sounds like a robust girl; it is Hardy the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair, a curl or long strand, is also called a tress.

clue.text: The pleasure which a usufruct implies

definitions.text: The pleasure which a usufruct implies

blocks.note: surface reading: delight in something
setter's reading: the legal right to use another's property, so the noun's legal sense of having use

explanation.walkthrough: A usufruct is a legal right to use and profit from property owned by someone else; lawyers call that the use of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both delight and, in law, the possession and use of a right or benefit.

clue.text: Such as the pronouncements of Joshua's successors

definitions.text: Such as the pronouncements of Joshua's successors

blocks.note: surface reading: the sayings of later leaders
setter's reading: the Book of Judges follows Joshua in the Bible, so their rulings are legal

explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Judges follows Joshua in the Old Testament, so his successors are judges, whose pronouncements are legal rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to law and the administration of justice.

clue.text: A sip Peter perhaps has before dinner

definitions.text: A sip Peter perhaps has before dinner

indicators.note: perhaps admits the words may come in another arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter enjoys a little sip of something ahead of his evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pre-dinner sip is exactly what the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink or small dish taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite is a starter of that kind.

clue.text: Bill supports Peter - he shows style

indicators.note: in a down clue whatever supports sits underneath, so it is written after the word it holds up

blocks.note: Peter Pan, J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up
AC is short for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bill backs up Peter, who has real flair.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece that supports another sits below it, so the bill comes after Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of manner, the dash and verve that marks someone with flair.

clue.text: Rent trouble creates a storm

blocks.note: rent means ripped
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: A dispute over rent payments stirs up a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money for housing; it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirlwind, a destructive rotating column of air.

clue.text: Note in duplicate about a resort in us

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the repeated note goes either side

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale, given twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical note, written twice, concerns a holiday town in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is the Florida city famed for its beaches, a holiday destination in the United States.

clue.text: Deity showing forbearance about the old city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: mercy is clemency
Ur, ancient Sumerian city, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A god shows clemency toward an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was the Roman messenger god, patron of trade and travellers.

clue.text: A Roman wayfarer who takes to the air

blocks.note: taken as written
viator is Latin for a traveller

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman traveller decides to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, a person who flies aircraft.

clue.text: One doomed by the Italian wife of albany

blocks.note: a goner is someone past saving
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian woman is ruined by her marriage to a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril, Lear's eldest daughter in Shakespeare's tragedy, is married to the Duke of Albany.

clue.text: Medal possibility though 50 disabled?

indicators.note: a possibility suggests one of several ways to arrange what precedes it

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wounded veteran might receive a medal despite being lame.
explanation.walkthrough: 50 is L in Roman numerals, a nudge toward the answer's opening letter; the letters come from the medal alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamed means crippled, made lame by injury, so unable to walk properly.

clue.text: A sometimes revolutionary type of road fuel, his, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the word before could be arranged another way

blocks.note: derv is British diesel for road vehicles
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A militant type is identified by the diesel in his car.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary suggests a political radical; it means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirling dervishes are Sufi Muslim mystics who spin round and round in ecstatic dance.

clue.text: Win back about 150 before the end

blocks.note: re means concerning
C is 100 and L is 50 in Roman numerals
an end is a goal

explanation.surface: A team needs to regain a lead of about 150 before the final whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover possession of what was lost.

clue.text: General fighting Indians captures many in a group

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: General Custer, killed at the Little Bighorn
L, 50 in Roman numerals, stands for a large number

explanation.surface: An American general at war with the Sioux takes lots of prisoners together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a bunch of similar things gathered closely together.

clue.text: Enter performer one found in the music centre

definitions.text: one found in the music centre

blocks.note: to enter details is to log them
a player is an actor or musician

explanation.surface: A performer makes an entrance at the concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Music centre sounds like a venue; it is the combined stereo unit of hi-fi days.
explanation.definitionFit: A music centre was an all-in-one stereo combining radio, cassette deck and turntable.
